mainTopic: Which items in the משנה are forbidden for benefit, and their sources: the מצורע's bird, שער נזיר, פטר חמור, בשר בחלב, and חולין slaughtered in the עזרה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of how we know which of the מצורע's two birds is permitted. The claim that living creatures are never forbidden is challenged twice, first with מוקצה ונעבד and then by רבי ירמיה with רובע ונרבע. It is finally reworded: most living creatures are not forbidden. דבי רבי ישמעאל learns the same thing from 'השדה', and רבא learns it from the idea that the Torah would not create a תקלה. The גמרא then goes through the items in the משנה that cannot be used for קידושין. שער נזיר is forbidden because the hair's growth is 'קדוש', though it cannot be redeemed like הקדש. פטר חמור is explained as being after עריפה, so everyone agrees it is forbidden. בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit because the פסוק is written three times, against רבי שמעון בן יהודה. For חולין slaughtered in the עזרה, רבי יוחנן's comparison is knocked down, and אביי brings a ברייתא that forbids slaughtering them and even eating them. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge: Some living animals are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that living creatures are never forbidden, pointing to מוקצה and נעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about an animal set aside for idol worship, or an animal that was itself worshipped? Those are living creatures, and they are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier answer that we never find a living animal that is forbidden. It brings two examples of living animals that are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said the sent-away bird must be the permitted one because living creatures are never forbidden. If מוקצה and נעבד are living and forbidden, that rule seems false. Then the proof about the bird falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside to be offered to an idol
An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol
Living creatures
They are forbidden

phrases.english: An animal set aside for an idol, and an animal that was worshipped,
which are living creatures, and yet they are forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּקְצֶה וְנֶעֱבָד, דְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִינְהוּ וַאֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier statement, given just before this passage, that living creatures are never forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that we never find living creatures that are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: מוקצה and נעבד are living animals, and they are forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: Forbidden only for the Altar
steps.stepSummary: מוקצה and נעבד are forbidden only as קרבנות. An ordinary person may still benefit from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they are forbidden, it is only for the Most High (as offerings). For an ordinary person, they are completely permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. It explains that מוקצה and נעבד are not forbidden in the sense that matters here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about a ban on any benefit at all. מוקצה and נעבד are banned only from the מזבח, and an ordinary person may still use them. So they do not disprove the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For the Most High: for use as an offering in the בית המקדש
For an ordinary person's use
Completely permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think מוקצה and נעבד are fine for everything. They are forbidden as קרבנות. The point is only that an ordinary person may benefit from them.

phrases.english: When they are forbidden, it is for the Most High,
but for an ordinary person, they are completely permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲסִירִי – לְגָבוֹהַּ, לְהֶדְיוֹט – מִישְׁרֵא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the kind of prohibition: forbidden only for the מזבח, not a ban on all benefit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוקצה and נעבד seemed to be fully forbidden living animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are forbidden only as offerings. An ordinary person may benefit, so the rule still stands.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's challenge: רובע ונרבע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה points to an animal involved in a forbidden relation, judged by witnesses. It is living and fully forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: But an animal that had relations with a person, either way, in front of witnesses, is a living creature, and it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a stronger example that cannot be answered the same way. This animal is forbidden for everyone, not just for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 2 worked because מוקצה and נעבד are still allowed for ordinary use. רובע ונרבע, once judged with witnesses, is forbidden for any benefit at all. So the rule 'living creatures are never forbidden' really does break.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, raises a strong challenge
An animal that had relations with a woman
An animal that a man had relations with
Before witnesses, so it can be judged in בית דין

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objects to it:
But there is an animal that copulated with a person, or that a person copulated with, before witnesses,
which are living creatures, and yet they are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new counterexample that the answer of step 2 cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that living creatures are never forbidden, even as defended in step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רובע ונרבע is a living animal that is forbidden for any benefit, not only for the מזבח.

steps.title: Reworded: Most living creatures are not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The statement is fixed to say that most living creatures are not forbidden, so we can rely on the normal pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: We do not find that most living creatures are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the claim of 'never' and rewords the rule as 'not most.' This saves the reasoning about the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is now about what usually happens, so a few exceptions like רובע ונרבע do not break it. Since most living animals are permitted, we assume the living, sent-away bird is the permitted one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces a corrected version
We have not found
Most, the majority

steps.whatToRemember: The final version is: most living creatures are not forbidden. So the bird that stays alive and is sent away is the permitted one.

phrases.english: Rather: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצִינוּ רוֹב בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים שֶׁאֲסוּרִים.
phrases.english: We have not found most living creatures to be forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the original statement to avoid רבי ירמיה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the original statement, from 'never' to 'not most'
steps.terutzMaskana: Most living creatures are not forbidden. Exceptions do not undo the assumption.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: The bird is like a field
steps.stepSummary: A second source: the bird is sent 'to the field,' and just as a field is permitted, so is the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The פסוק says 'And he shall send it over the open field.' It is like a field. Just as a field is permitted, this bird is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to know the sent-away bird is permitted. This one comes straight from a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reasoning from what is usual among animals, this source compares the bird to the field it is sent to. A field is permitted for use, so the bird is too.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
The פסוק
Field
Permitted

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For the verse says: "And he shall send it over the open field":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:7

phrases.english: like a field: just as a field is permitted,
so too, this bird is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent source for the same conclusion as רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sent-away bird is permitted, learned by comparing it to the field.

steps.title: Challenge: 'Field' teaches where to throw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the word 'field' is needed for a different law: the bird must be thrown from the city out to the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this word 'field' come to teach that? It is needed for what was taught: 'Field' teaches that one may not stand in יפו and throw it to the sea, or in גבת and throw it to the desert, and may not stand outside the city and throw it into the city. Rather, he must stand in the city and throw it outside the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges דבי רבי ישמעאל. It argues that the word 'field' is already used up by another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא learns from 'field' exactly where the bird must be sent: from inside the city toward a field outside the wall. It cannot go to the sea or the desert. If the word teaches that, how can it also teach that the bird is permitted?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that what it comes to teach?
It is needed for
As was taught in a ברייתא
City wall

phrases.english: Does this word "field" come for this?
That word is needed for that which was taught:
"Field": that he may not stand in Yafo and throw it to the sea,
or stand in Gevat and throw it to the desert,
and that he may not stand outside the city
and throw it into the city.
Rather, whenever he stands in the city
and throws it outside the wall, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of דבי רבי ישמעאל from the word 'field'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already needed to teach where the bird is thrown, so it cannot also teach that the bird is permitted.

steps.title: Answer: 'The field' teaches both
steps.stepSummary: The extra 'ה' in 'השדה' shows that the word teaches two lessons: where to throw and that the bird is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? If so, let the פסוק write 'field.' Why does it say 'the field'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer of דבי רבי ישמעאל. The extra letter ה lets the word teach both laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain 'שדה' would have been enough to teach where to throw the bird. The Torah wrote 'השדה,' with an extra ה, so there is room for a second lesson: the bird is permitted like a field. Both teachings come from the same word.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other view: how does it answer?
If so
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: דבי רבי ישמעאל learns from 'השדה' both where the bird must be thrown and that it is permitted for benefit.

phrases.english: And the other view?
phrases.notes: The other view is דבי רבי ישמעאל: how would they answer this?

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write "field";
what is the point of "the field"?
Conclude two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק (the ה) allows a second lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'field' teaches only where to throw the bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'השדה' teaches both where to throw the bird and that the bird is permitted.

steps.title: רבא: The Torah Would Not Command a Trap
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source for why the bird that is sent away is permitted. The Torah would not tell us to send off a forbidden bird that people could find and eat by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: The Torah did not say 'send it away' so that it would become a stumbling block.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new, logical way to know that the bird sent free is permitted, instead of the 'field' derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the freed bird were forbidden, letting it fly away would set a trap: someone could catch it and eat it without knowing. Since the Torah commands 'שלח,' the bird must be permitted. רבא needs no extra letter in the פסוק, only common sense about how the Torah works.

keyTerms.meaning: Send away. The Torah's command to let the second bird go free.
A stumbling block, something that causes people to sin by mistake.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to show the freed bird is permitted: רבי יוחנן's reasoning that most living creatures are not forbidden, the 'השדה' derivation of דבי רבי ישמעאל, and רבא's rule that the Torah does not create a תקלה.

phrases.english: Rava says:
The Torah did not say "send away" for a stumbling block.
phrases.notes: If the freed bird were forbidden, someone might catch it and eat it by mistake. The Torah would not set up that kind of trap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logic-based alternative to the 'השדה' derivation of steps 5-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird sent free is permitted, because the Torah would not command sending away a forbidden bird that could cause a תקלה.

steps.title: Source for the נזיר's Hair Being Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, שער נזיר, and asks where we learn that benefit from it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a נזיר's hair. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that קידושין with a נזיר's hair does not work, which means the hair is forbidden for benefit. The גמרא wants to see the פסוק behind that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The hair of a נזיר, which grows during his נזירות.
From where do we know this? A request for a source.

phrases.english: With a nazirite's hair.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if a man is מקדש a woman with a נזיר's hair, she is not betrothed.

phrases.english: From where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new item in the list in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that benefit from שער נזיר is forbidden.

steps.title: The Hair's Growth Is Holy
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the נזיר 'shall be holy' while he lets his hair grow. This teaches that the growth itself is holy and forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: 'He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.' This means his growth shall be holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that links the word 'holy' to the growing hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'קדש יהיה' right next to the growing of the hair. The גמרא reads them together: the hair's growth is holy. Something holy is forbidden for personal benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says. Introduces a פסוק as a source.
His growth, the hair that grew.
Holy. The form the פסוק uses here.

phrases.english: As the verse states:
"He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:5

phrases.english: His growth shall be holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'קדש יהיה גדל פרע' teaches that the hair's growth is holy, and so forbidden.

steps.title: Can the Hair Be Redeemed Like הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: If the hair is 'holy' like הקדש, it should be redeemable: its holiness would pass to the money and the hair would become ordinary. That is not the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as הקדש passes its holiness onto its money and itself becomes ordinary, so too a נזיר's hair should pass its holiness onto its money and become ordinary!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to הקדש by pointing to a rule of הקדש that does not apply to a נזיר's hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקדש can be redeemed: you pay money, the money becomes holy, and the item becomes חולין. If 'holy' makes the hair like הקדש, the hair should be redeemable too. But we know it is not, so the comparison seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property, הקדש.
Transfers its holiness onto the money paid to redeem it.
Becomes ordinary, no longer holy.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה קֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו,
phrases.english: If so, just as consecrated property transfers its sanctity to its money,
and becomes non-sacred,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׂעַר נָזִיר תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו
phrases.english: so too a nazirite's hair should transfer its sanctity to its money
and become non-sacred!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה קֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation of step 10 by pushing the comparison to הקדש further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of שער נזיר to הקדש through the word 'holy.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the hair is like הקדש, it should share הקדש's ability to be redeemed. It does not, so the comparison seems wrong.

steps.title: קדוש, Not קודש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'קדוש,' not 'קודש,' the word used for הקדש. So the hair is holy, but it does not take on the redemption rules of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we read 'קודש'? We read 'קדוש'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to the exact form of the word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קודש' is the term for consecrated property, and that would bring in the rules of redemption. The פסוק uses 'קדוש,' a different form, which only tells us the hair is forbidden. It does not make the hair into הקדש with all its laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we read? A rhetorical question about the wording of a פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: Both words mean 'holy.' The answer depends only on the form: 'קודש' is the term for הקדש, while 'קדוש' simply describes something as holy.
steps.whatToRemember: שער נזיר is forbidden for benefit because of 'קדוש יהיה,' but it cannot be redeemed, because the פסוק did not say 'קודש.'

phrases.english: Do we read "kodesh"?
phrases.notes: 'קודש' is the word the Torah uses for consecrated property.

phrases.english: We read "kadosh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording of the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Holy' makes the hair exactly like הקדש, so it should be redeemable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק says 'קדוש,' not 'קודש,' so the hair is forbidden but not redeemable like הקדש.

steps.title: Does the משנה Go Against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says קידושין with a פטר חמור does not work. A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור, so the משנה seems to follow only רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a firstborn donkey. Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי שמעון? For it was taught: benefit from a firstborn donkey is forbidden, this is the view of רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the פטר חמור case in the משנה and suggests that it fits only one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a פטר חמור as forbidden, so it is worth nothing for קידושין. But רבי שמעון says benefit from it is permitted. That would mean the משנה follows רבי יהודה and not רבי שמעון, which the גמרא would prefer to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey. It must be redeemed with a lamb, or its neck is broken.
Shall we say? Introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject.
Forbidden for any benefit.

phrases.english: With a firstborn donkey.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה again: קידושין with a פטר חמור does not work.

phrases.english: Shall we say the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon?
As it is taught:
A firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit;
this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה, פטר חמור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that קידושין with a פטר חמור does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור, so by his view קידושין with it should work. The משנה then seems to follow only רבי יהודה.

steps.title: After the Neck Is Broken, Everyone Agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the משנה is talking about a פטר חמור after its neck was broken. Then everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The משנה is talking about after the neck was broken, and that is everyone's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case in the משנה so it fits both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת in the ברייתא is about a living פטר חמור. Once its neck has been broken, even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden for benefit. So the משנה fits everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck. Done to a פטר חמור that was not redeemed.
Everyone's view. All opinions agree.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of פטר חמור is after עריפה, when all agree it is forbidden. So the משנה fits רבי שמעון too.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It is after its neck was broken,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה is talking about a donkey that was not redeemed, so its neck was broken.

phrases.english: and that is everyone's opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לְאַחַר עֲרִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about a living פטר חמור, so it goes against רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about after עריפה, when even רבי שמעון forbids it.

steps.title: What is the source that meat cooked in milk is forbidden for benefit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, בשר בחלב, and asks how we know that benefit from it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat cooked in milk: from where do we know it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the משנה's list, בשר בחלב, and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says קידושין with בשר בחלב does not work. That only makes sense if benefit from it is forbidden. So the גמרא wants a source for an איסור הנאה, not just a ban on eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat cooked together with milk
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Meat in milk: from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the next item from the משנה, and asking for the source that you may not benefit from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from פטר חמור to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that benefit from בשר בחלב is forbidden.

steps.title: The verse appears three times: eating, benefit, cooking
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that the Torah writes 'do not cook a kid in its mother's milk' three times, once each for eating, benefit, and cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk' is written three times. One is for the ban on eating, one for the ban on benefit, and one for the ban on cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. Because the Torah repeats the פסוק three times, each time teaches a separate איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat words for no reason. So the three repeats are split into three איסורים, and one of them is the איסור הנאה. That is the source the משנה needs.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
Three times
A ban on getting any benefit
A ban on the act of cooking

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the three separate איסורים of בשר בחלב: eating, benefit and cooking.

phrases.english: For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:19; שמות 34:26; דברים 14:21.

phrases.english: is written three times:
one for the ban on eating,
and one for the ban on benefit,
and one for the ban on cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three repeats of the פסוק teach three איסורים, one of which is an איסור הנאה.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן יהודה, who holds that בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. He learns this from the word 'holy' in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. For it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says that meat in milk is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. It says 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God, you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk,' and elsewhere it says 'You shall be holy people to Me.' Just as there it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, so too here it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different תנא disagrees with our משנה. רבי שמעון בן יהודה permits benefit from בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'holy.' The second one is about forbidden meat that may still be thrown to the dogs, so benefit is allowed there. רבי שמעון בן יהודה links the two and allows benefit from בשר בחלב too, so by his view קידושין with it would work.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow this תנא
Permitted for benefit
Just as there… so too here (a comparison between two פסוקים)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question against the משנה. The גמרא is simply saying which תנא the משנה follows. It follows the school of רבי ישמעאל, not רבי שמעון בן יהודה.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in line with this tanna.
phrases.notes: "This tanna" is the one about to be quoted, רבי שמעון בן יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: For it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says:
Meat in milk is forbidden to eat
but permitted for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
phrases.english: as it says: "For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God;
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21.

phrases.english: you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk,"
and elsewhere it says:
"And you shall be holy people to Me."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30, a פסוק about forbidden meat that the Torah says to throw to the dogs.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה
phrases.english: Just as there it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: – אַף כָּאן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.english: so too here it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the source in step 16 is not accepted by every תנא, and says which side our משנה takes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows the view that בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit, against רבי שמעון בן יהודה, who permits it.

steps.title: What is the source for non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next item, חולין שנשחטו בעזרה, and asks for the source that benefit from them is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the עזרה: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary animals are normally fine to use. The משנה says that if they were slaughtered in the עזרה, קידושין with them does not work. So the גמרא wants to know where this איסור הנאה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-sacred animals
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
From where are these things known?

phrases.english: And non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
From where are these things known?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from בשר בחלב to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that benefit from חולין slaughtered in the עזרה is forbidden.

steps.title: Mine in My place, yours in your place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי מאיר‎: ה׳'s animals belong in ה׳'s place and yours in your place. Just as קדשים slaughtered outside are forbidden, חולין slaughtered inside are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: The Torah said, slaughter Mine in My place, and yours in your place. Just as Mine in your place is forbidden, so too yours in My place is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by comparing two opposite mistakes. Bringing קדשים outside is forbidden, and so is bringing חולין inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Mine' means קדשים, which must be slaughtered in the עזרה. 'Yours' means ordinary animals, which belong outside. Since קדשים slaughtered outside are forbidden for benefit, the reverse case, חולין slaughtered inside, is forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter what is Mine in My place
And what is yours in your place

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
The Torah said: Slaughter what is Mine in My place.
phrases.notes: "Mine" means קרבנות, and "My place" means inside the עזרה.

phrases.english: And what is yours, in your place.
Just as Mine in your place is forbidden,
so too yours in My place is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison: just as קדשים slaughtered outside are forbidden, חולין slaughtered inside the עזרה are forbidden.

steps.title: Should slaughtering חולין in the עזרה also bring כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the comparison further. Slaughtering קדשים outside is punished with כרת, so should slaughtering חולין inside be punished with כרת too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as Mine in your place is punished with כרת, should yours in My place also be punished with כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's comparison. If the two cases are equal, they should be equal in punishment as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה carries כרת. If חולין in the עזרה are learned from that case, we would expect כרת there too. That does not seem right, so the comparison needs a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Punished with כרת, being cut off
If so, just as… (pushing a comparison further)

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה שֶׁלִּי בְּשֶׁלָּךְ עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: If so, just as Mine in your place is punished with karet,
should yours in My place also be punished with karet?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה שֶׁלִּי בְּשֶׁלָּךְ עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's comparison between קדשים outside and חולין inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would also bring the punishment of כרת to חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.

steps.title: כרת only for a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about כרת speaks about a קרבן, so כרת applies only to a קרבן slaughtered outside, not to חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he did not bring it to the entrance of the אהל מועד to offer a קרבן to ה׳… and he shall be cut off.' For a קרבן there is כרת. For חולין slaughtered in the עזרה there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק limits כרת to a קרבן. So the comparison teaches the איסור but not the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that gives כרת mentions a 'קרבן' clearly. That word limits כרת to קדשים slaughtered outside. The איסור הנאה on חולין in the עזרה still stands from the comparison, but without כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the משכן
And he shall be cut off

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק limits כרת to a קרבן slaughtered outside, so חולין slaughtered in the עזרה carry no כרת. The next step uses this very difference to knock down רבי יוחנן's whole comparison.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4.

phrases.english: to offer an offering to ה׳… and he shall be cut off,"
for an offering, one is punished with karet;

phrases.aramaic: עַל חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה – אֵין עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: for non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard, one is not punished with karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison using the wording of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison would make חולין in the עזרה equal in every way, including כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'קרבן' limits כרת to קדשים slaughtered outside. The comparison gives only the איסור to חולין in the עזרה.

steps.title: The comparison breaks down because of כרת
steps.stepSummary: Since slaughtering קדשים outside carries כרת, it is more severe and cannot serve as a model for חולין slaughtered inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what is special about My animals in your place? It is punished with כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבי יוחנן's comparison (step 19). Slaughtering קדשים outside is stricter, so we cannot learn the benefit prohibition for חולין from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 showed that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה do not carry כרת. That difference now becomes a weakness. Maybe the benefit prohibition exists only because slaughtering קדשים outside is so severe (כרת). If so, the lighter case of חולין inside would stay permitted for benefit, and we are left without a source again.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted. This points out a difference that breaks a comparison.
What is special about...? This is the standard opening for showing that the source case is stricter.
Punished with כרת, being cut off spiritually

steps.confusionAlert: Step 21 did not settle the matter. It only explained why there is no כרת for חולין. Here the גמרא uses that very difference to tear down the whole comparison.

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What is special about Mine in yours?
phrases.notes: ה׳ is speaking: 'My animals (קדשים) slaughtered in your place (outside).' This is the language of step 19.

phrases.english: That it is punished with כרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the difference from step 21 (no כרת for חולין) into a refutation of the whole comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's comparison between קדשים outside and חולין inside (step 19)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case (קדשים outside) carries כרת and is stricter. A stricter case cannot teach a prohibition for a lighter case.

steps.title: אביי offers a new source: three extra words
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to three פסוקים about שלמים that each say 'it' unnecessarily, and asks what they come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: from here. 'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.' Three extra verses. Why does the Torah say them?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first source fell, אביי brings a new one. He sets it up by pointing out three extra words in the Torah and asking what they teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three פסוקים about שלמים (cattle, sheep, goat) adds the word 'אותו' ('it'), which seems unnecessary. The question 'מה תלמוד לומר' signals that a ברייתא will now explain what these extra words come to include. This step is a setup for the derivation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra verses, words the Torah did not need to say
Why does the Torah need to say this? It asks what an extra word teaches.

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said: from here:
'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.'
Three extra verses.
Why does the verse need to say them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the refuted source with a new one based on extra words in the Torah.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the three extra words 'אותו' in the פסוקים of שלמים, as a ברייתא will explain.

steps.title: Far from the מקדש you slaughter, but not near it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'כי ירחק ממך המקום' that חולין are slaughtered only far from the מקדש, not in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says: 'If the place is far from you… then you shall slaughter.' When you are far from the place you slaughter, but you do not slaughter in a near place. This excludes חולין, which may not be slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lays down its basic rule. The Torah allowed slaughtering ordinary meat 'far away,' which shows that you may not slaughter it 'nearby,' in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק permits slaughtering for ordinary meat when you are far from the מקדש. The ברייתא reads this as a limit: only far away, not close by. This gives the basic prohibition against slaughtering חולין in the עזרה, which the next steps will widen.

keyTerms.meaning: Far from the place, meaning far from the בית המקדש
This excludes...
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
'If the place is far from you… then you shall slaughter.'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:21

phrases.english: When far from the place, you slaughter,
but you do not slaughter in a near place,
which excludes חולין, that they may not be slaughtered in the עזרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי יִרְחַק מִמְּךָ הַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that will explain the extra words from step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין may not be slaughtered in the עזרה, learned from 'כי ירחק ממך המקום'.

steps.title: Including blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The basic rule covers healthy animals fit for a קרבן. Blemished animals are included because they belong to a kind that can be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about unblemished animals fit to be offered. How do we include blemished animals? I include blemished animals, since they are of a kind that is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the rule also covers blemished animals, which can never be offered. It answers yes, using simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the rule applies only to animals that look like they could be קרבנות. A blemished animal still belongs to a species that is used for קרבנות (cattle, sheep, goats), so it is included without needing a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished animals
Blemished animals, unfit for a קרבן
A species that is fit to be offered

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא תְּמִימִים הָרְאוּיִם לִיקָּרֵב,
phrases.english: I only know about unblemished animals that are fit to be offered.
From where do we include blemished animals?
I include blemished animals,
since they are of a kind that is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא תְּמִימִים הָרְאוּיִם לִיקָּרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule from step 24 to blemished animals by logic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on slaughtering חולין in the עזרה cover blemished animals?

steps.title: Including wild animals (חיה)
steps.stepSummary: Wild animals are never offered, but they are included because they need שחיטה just like domestic animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we include the wild animal? I include the wild animal, since it needs שחיטה like a domestic animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. Wild animals are never קרבנות, yet they are still included by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חיה is not even a species fit for a קרבן, so the reason from step 25 does not work. A new link is found instead: a חיה becomes permitted to eat through שחיטה, exactly like a בהמה. That shared feature is enough to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, such as a deer
A domestic animal
Kosher slaughter

phrases.english: From where do we include the wild animal?
I include the wild animal,
since it is made fit by slaughter, like a domestic animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule further, from blemished animals to wild animals, using a new point of similarity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban cover a חיה, which is never offered?

steps.title: Including birds through the three extra words
steps.stepSummary: Birds cannot be included by logic, so the three extra words 'אותו' are needed to include them. This explains the question from step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we include birds? The verse says: 'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.'
steps.whatsHappening: For birds there is no logical link left, so the ברייתא uses the three extra words. This closes the loop and answers the 'מה תלמוד לומר' from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons that worked for blemished animals and wild animals do not reach birds, because the Torah does not mention שחיטה for birds, so the extra 'אותו' words in the three פסוקים of שלמים are needed to include them. As a result, no kind of חולין may be slaughtered in the עזרה. The ברייתא then goes on, in the next step, to ask about eating the meat after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds
To include

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's comparison failed because of כרת. אביי's source is a ברייתא. 'כי ירחק' bans slaughtering חולין in the עזרה. Logic adds blemished animals and wild animals, and the three extra words 'אותו' add birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא builds up step by step. It uses logic as far as logic can go, and uses the extra words only where logic gives out. This shows why the three 'אותו's are not wasted words.

phrases.english: From where do we include birds?
The verse teaches:
'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.'
phrases.notes: These are the same three extra words אביי pointed to in step 23. Here we finally see what they teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָעוֹפוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the widening of the rule and ties it back to the extra words from step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three extra words 'אותו' include even birds in the ban on slaughtering חולין in the עזרה. The ברייתא continues in step 28 with the ban on eating such meat after the fact.

steps.title: Even after the fact, the meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether חולין slaughtered in the עזרה might be allowed if it already happened. It learns from the פסוק that only meat slaughtered far away may be eaten, so this meat is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person should not slaughter there, but if he did, the meat is allowed. So the פסוק says: 'If the place is far from you, you shall slaughter and you shall eat.' What you slaughter far away, you may eat. What you slaughter close by, you may not eat. This excludes חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second layer to the rule from step 24. Slaughtering חולין in the עזרה is not just something to avoid; if it happens, the meat may not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 only taught that one should not slaughter חולין in the עזרה. Here the ברייתא reads the words 'slaughter… and eat' together: eating is allowed only for what was slaughtered 'far.' That turns the rule into an איסור on eating the meat, even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought' — introduces a possible mistaken conclusion
'The פסוק teaches' — introduces the verse that settles the question
Far from the Place, meaning outside the מקדש
'Excluding' — what the פסוק comes to leave out
Ordinary, non-holy animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 24. Step 24 said 'don't slaughter there.' This step says 'and if you did, you can't eat it.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are forbidden to eat. The rest of the סוגיא asks which animals this איסור covers.

phrases.english: One might think: he should not slaughter there,
but if he did slaughter, it would be permitted?
phrases.notes: Meaning permitted to eat, after the fact.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches: "If the place is too far from you..."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:21

phrases.english: "...then you shall slaughter... and you shall eat",

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ בְּרִחוּק מָקוֹם – אַתָּה אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: what you slaughter far from the Place, you may eat,
but you may not eat
what you slaughter in a near place,
phrases.notes: A 'near place' means inside the מקדש itself.

phrases.english: excluding non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִשְׁחוֹט, וְאִם שָׁחַט יְהֵא מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 24. It moves from 'don't slaughter there' to 'if you did, you may not eat it.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין slaughtered in the עזרה may not be eaten, even after the fact, because the פסוק permits eating only what is slaughtered far from the מקדש.

steps.title: Does the rule cover more than unblemished animals?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts its next question: so far the rule only clearly covers unblemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I only know this rule for unblemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא points out what its proof covers so far, which prepares the next move: widening the rule to other animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'near place' in the פסוק is where קרבנות are brought. So the clearest case is an animal that could itself be a קרבן, a healthy unblemished one. The ברייתא now asks whether animals that could not be offered are also included.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have…' — a formula saying the source so far covers only this case, leading to a widening of the rule
Unblemished, healthy animals that are fit to be a קרבן

phrases.english: And I have derived this only for unblemished animals,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the איסור on eating, the ברייתא now checks which animals it applies to. It is repeating for the eating ban the same widening that steps 25–27 did for the slaughter ban, and this continues on the next amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the איסור on eating חולין slaughtered in the עזרה apply only to unblemished animals, or to other animals too?
